title: Lesson 1: Speaking Politely and Choosing Appropriate Words
summary: The same message can welcome people or create tension. Choose words that are clear, respectful and suitable for clients, colleagues and supervisors.

items.label: Duration
items.body: 45–60 minutes

items.label: Participants
items.body: All Zura Spa staff

items.label: Focus
items.body: Professional language, respectful communication, clarity and positive workplace interactions

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: Imagine a client arrives at Zura Spa for a scheduled massage session.
She approaches the receptionist and asks whether her therapist is available.
The receptionist responds: "Can't you see I'm busy? Just sit down and wait."
Now imagine the receptionist responding differently: "Good afternoon. Welcome to Zura Spa. Please have a seat while I confirm that your therapist is ready."
Both responses communicate that the client needs to wait.
However, the words used create completely different experiences.
The first response may make the client feel unwelcome or disrespected.
The second communicates courtesy, professionalism and consideration.
The same principle applies when communicating with colleagues, supervisors and management.
The words we choose can either strengthen relationships or create unnecessary tension.
At Zura Spa, employees must learn to communicate clearly, politely and appropriately, regardless of their position or responsibilities.

sections.title: 2. What does speaking politely mean?
paragraphs: Speaking politely means communicating in a way that demonstrates respect, consideration and professionalism.
It involves choosing words that express your message clearly without unnecessary insults, hostility, humiliation or aggression.
Polite communication does not require employees to agree with everyone or avoid difficult conversations.
It means delivering messages in a respectful and constructive manner.
Politeness is not weakness. It is the ability to communicate effectively while respecting other people.

sections.title: Examples of polite communication
list: Greeting people appropriately.
Using courteous expressions such as "please" and "thank you."
Making requests without unnecessary demands.
Giving corrections without insults.
Expressing disagreement respectfully.
Apologising when appropriate.
Avoiding offensive or humiliating language.
Speaking clearly without unnecessary shouting.
Adjusting language to suit the situation and audience.

sections.title: 3. Why appropriate words matter at Zura Spa
1. Words influence client experience
paragraphs: Clients expect a welcoming, comfortable and professional environment.
Courteous communication helps clients feel respected from the moment they contact or visit Zura Spa.

sections.title: 2. Words strengthen teamwork
paragraphs: Employees cooperate more effectively when they communicate with respect rather than hostility.

sections.title: 3. Words prevent unnecessary conflict
paragraphs: Many workplace disagreements become worse because of the language used rather than the original issue.

sections.title: 4. Words improve understanding
paragraphs: Clear, specific language reduces confusion, assumptions and mistakes.

sections.title: 5. Words reflect professionalism
paragraphs: The way employees speak influences how clients, colleagues and management perceive the organisation.

sections.title: 4. The difference between polite and impolite language
paragraphs: These examples show that employees can communicate the same message without unnecessary disrespect.
table: "Please, could you assist me with this?"
"This needs to be corrected. Let me explain the procedure."
"I see it differently. Can we consider another approach?"
"Could you please clarify what you mean?"
"Let me check what can be done."
"I noticed this issue. How can we prevent it next time?"
"I can't do it. Leave me alone."
"I'm unable to assist right now because I'm attending to another responsibility."
"I understand your concern. I'll review it."
"I'm sorry for the way I spoke. I should have handled it better."

sections.title: Principle 1: Think before you speak
paragraphs: Before responding, consider whether your words are necessary, accurate, respectful and appropriate.
list: Is what I am about to say true?
Is it relevant to the situation?
Is it respectful?
Could I express it more clearly?
Am I addressing the issue or attacking the person?

sections.title: Principle 2: Choose words that communicate respect
paragraphs: Simple expressions such as "please," "thank you," "excuse me" and "I appreciate your help" can make workplace interactions more pleasant.
However, politeness is more than using courteous expressions.
A person can say "please" while speaking sarcastically or aggressively.
The entire message should demonstrate respect.

sections.title: Principle 3: Be clear and specific
paragraphs: Avoid vague instructions or statements that leave others confused.
Unclear: "Arrange everything properly."
Clearer: "Please replace the clean towels, check the massage oil and ensure the treatment room is ready before the next appointment."
Clear communication improves accountability and reduces mistakes.

sections.title: Principle 4: Avoid personal attacks
paragraphs: When correcting someone, focus on the behaviour or task.
Personal attack: "You are lazy."
Professional correction: "The room was not prepared before the scheduled appointment. Please ensure it is ready on time."

sections.title: Principle 5: Adapt your language to the audience
paragraphs: The language used in casual conversations with friends may not always be appropriate when speaking to clients, supervisors or colleagues.
Employees should use language that is understandable, respectful and suitable for the professional setting.
At Zura Spa, client-facing communication should be clear and courteous. Avoid slang or expressions that could confuse or offend clients.

sections.title: Principle 6: Be firm without being rude
paragraphs: Employees may need to refuse inappropriate requests, enforce boundaries or communicate difficult information.
They should do so clearly and professionally.
Example: "I'm sorry, but we do not offer that service at Zura Spa."
This is more appropriate than insulting or humiliating the person making the request.

sections.title: Principle 7: Take responsibility for your words
paragraphs: If you speak inappropriately, acknowledge it.
A sincere apology should not be followed by excuses that shift responsibility to the other person.
Example: "I spoke harshly earlier. I apologise. I should have explained the situation more respectfully."

sections.title: 6. The power of tone and delivery
paragraphs: Words are important, but the way they are spoken also matters.
Consider the sentence: "Please come here."
It may sound respectful when spoken calmly.
The same sentence may sound threatening or impatient when shouted aggressively.
Employees should avoid unnecessary shouting, eye-rolling, threatening gestures and deliberately dismissive expressions.
Important: A calm tone should not be confused with speaking too quietly to be understood. The goal is clear, respectful communication.

items.label: Tone
items.body: The emotional quality of your voice.

items.label: Volume
items.body: How loudly or softly you speak.

items.label: Pace
items.body: How quickly you speak.

items.label: Facial expression
items.body: Whether your expression matches the message.

items.label: Body language
items.body: Whether your posture and gestures communicate openness or hostility.

sections.title: 7. Speaking politely to clients
paragraphs: Every client interaction contributes to the Zura Spa experience.
This includes phone calls, WhatsApp messages, reception conversations, treatment-room communication and follow-up discussions.
If a client becomes threatening, harassing or abusive, employees should follow the appropriate safety and escalation procedures.
Employees should not promise refunds, compensation or outcomes they are not authorised to approve.

items.label: A. Welcoming a client
items.body: "Good afternoon. Welcome to Zura Spa. How may I assist you?"

items.label: B. Asking a client to wait
items.body: "Thank you for your patience. Please give us a few minutes while we prepare for your session."

items.label: C. Explaining a delay
items.body: "I apologise for the delay. We're working to have everything ready as soon as possible. Thank you for your understanding."

items.label: D. Clarifying a client's preference
items.body: "Would you prefer light, firm or deep pressure? Please let me know if you would like any adjustment during the session."

items.label: E. Declining an inappropriate request
items.body: "Zura Spa provides professional massage services only. We do not offer that service."

items.label: F. Responding to a complaint
items.body: "Thank you for bringing this to our attention. I'm sorry your experience did not meet expectations. Let me report this so we can review the concern."

sections.title: 8. Speaking politely to colleagues
paragraphs: Professional language is equally important when communicating with coworkers.
Some employees are courteous to clients but speak rudely to colleagues.
This is inconsistent with a healthy workplace culture.
Lesson: Colleagues deserve the same basic courtesy that employees are expected to show clients.

items.label: Requesting assistance
items.body: Instead of: "Come and help me. What are you doing?" Say: "Please, are you available to help me prepare the room?"

items.label: Addressing a mistake
items.body: Instead of: "You always mess things up." Say: "I noticed an error in the preparation. Let's correct it before the client arrives."

items.label: Disagreeing with a suggestion
items.body: Instead of: "That idea doesn't make sense." Say: "I understand your suggestion, but I have a concern about how it would work."

items.label: Declining additional work
items.body: Instead of: "That's not my job. Leave me alone." Say: "I'm currently handling another task. Please check with the supervisor about who can assist."

sections.title: 9. Speaking politely to supervisors and management
paragraphs: Employees should communicate professionally when receiving instructions, giving updates, raising concerns or requesting clarification.
Supervisors and management must also communicate respectfully with employees. Authority does not justify insults, threats or humiliation.

items.label: When receiving instructions
items.body: "Understood. I'll attend to it."

items.label: When instructions are unclear
items.body: "Please, could you clarify the expected outcome?"

items.label: When a deadline may not be achievable
items.body: "I may need additional time to complete this properly. Can we review the priorities?"

items.label: When disagreeing with a decision
items.body: "I understand the decision, but I would appreciate an opportunity to explain my concern."

items.label: When reporting a mistake
items.body: "I made an error while completing the task. I have identified the issue and would like guidance on the next step."

sections.title: 10. Words and expressions employees should avoid
paragraphs: Certain expressions can unnecessarily damage workplace relationships.
Employees should replace these expressions with clear statements about the actual issue and the action required.

sections.title: 11. Practical communication method: The CLEAR approach

items.label: C — Calm
items.body: Manage your tone and avoid speaking impulsively.

items.label: L — Listen
items.body: Understand the other person's message before responding.

items.label: E — Express
items.body: State your message clearly and respectfully.

items.label: A — Ask
items.body: Seek clarification rather than making assumptions.

items.label: R — Resolve
items.body: Focus on the next appropriate action or solution.

sections.title: CLEAR example
paragraphs: A therapist discovers that the next client has been scheduled earlier than expected.
Instead of saying: "Why did you people change the time without telling me?"
She could say: "I noticed the appointment time has changed. Could you explain when the update was made? I need to confirm that the room can be ready."
This approach is calm, specific and solution-focused.

sections.title: Case study A: The rude receptionist
paragraphs: A client calls Zura Spa to ask about available massage services.
The receptionist is busy and responds: "All the information is online. Go and check it."
Expected lesson: Employees should communicate courteously and offer reasonable assistance or an appropriate alternative.
list: What is inappropriate about the response?
How might the client interpret it?
How could the receptionist respond more professionally?
What should the receptionist do if she is genuinely too busy to answer immediately?

sections.title: Case study B: The frustrated therapist
paragraphs: A therapist discovers that another employee has not replenished the treatment supplies.
She says: "You're so careless. You never do anything properly."
Expected lesson: Address the task and the required correction without attacking the person.
list: Which words make the statement disrespectful?
How could the message be communicated more clearly?
What action should the employees take?
How can the issue be prevented from recurring?

sections.title: Case study C: The supervisor's instruction
paragraphs: A supervisor asks an employee to complete an urgent task.
The employee is already attending to another responsibility and responds: "Can't you see I'm busy? Stop disturbing me."
Expected lesson: Employees can communicate workload limitations respectfully and seek prioritisation.
list: Why is the response inappropriate?
What legitimate concern does the employee have?
How can she express that concern professionally?
What should the supervisor clarify?

sections.title: Case study D: The difficult client
paragraphs: A client complains that her massage session started later than expected.
The employee responds: "You're not the only customer here."
Expected lesson: Courteous language can help resolve complaints without dismissing legitimate concerns.
list: Why might the response escalate the complaint?
What could the employee say instead?
Why is acknowledging the client's concern important?
When should the matter be escalated to a supervisor?

sections.title: 13. Interactive assessment
paragraphs: Complete the Lesson 1 Knowledge Check at the bottom of this lesson. Choose an option, give your reason, then submit.
list: Which statement best describes polite workplace communication? Agreeing with everyone regardless of the situation / Expressing messages clearly and respectfully / Avoiding all difficult conversations

A colleague makes a mistake. Which response is most professional? The room is missing supplies. Please correct it before the next appointment. / You never do anything properly. / Everybody knows you're careless.
You are too busy to assist a colleague immediately. What should you say? Leave me alone. / That's your problem. / I'm completing another task. Can we arrange assistance through the supervisor?
A client complains about a delay. What is the best response? You're not the only client here. / I'm sorry for the delay. Let me check the situation and update you. / Stop complaining.

What does the CLEAR communication method encourage? Calmness, listening, clear expression, clarification and resolution / Speaking quickly to end conversations / Avoiding responsibility for difficult messages

sections.title: 14. Personal assignment
paragraphs: Each employee should answer the following questions in writing.
list: Explain what speaking politely means in your own words.
Identify five reasons appropriate language is important at Zura Spa.
Rewrite five rude workplace expressions into professional alternatives.
Explain the difference between being polite and being weak.
Describe how you would respond to a client who complains about a delay.
Explain why colleagues deserve the same basic courtesy as clients.
Describe the CLEAR communication method.
Identify three personal communication habits you intend to improve.

sections.title: 15. Seven-day professional speech challenge
table: Use clear and respectful language when making requests
Avoid unnecessary insults, sarcasm and dismissive expressions
Practise asking questions instead of making assumptions
Remain polite when frustrated or under pressure
Reflect on how your words affected workplace relationships

sections.title: 16. Final lesson and takeaway
paragraphs: The words employees use influence relationships, teamwork and client satisfaction.
At Zura Spa, every employee should communicate with courtesy, clarity and professionalism.
Speaking politely does not mean avoiding difficult conversations or pretending to agree with everyone.
It means expressing messages appropriately, respecting others and choosing words that help rather than unnecessarily harm.
Next topic: Listening Without Interrupting.

remember: Your words can encourage cooperation or create conflict. They can make a client feel welcomed or uncomfortable. They can help a colleague improve or make that colleague afraid to ask questions. Choose words that communicate respect, clarity and professionalism. The way you speak is part of the service you deliver and the team culture you help create.
